summary.en: Haitian police have retaken the national stadium from gangs after two years of control, while Salvadoran missiles and ground forces struck a gang hideout, destroying the Mawozo headquarters and killing about 20 gang members, prompting the Haitian prime minister to praise President Bukele. The United Nations reported more than 1,000 people killed between July and September, and the UN chief condemned a recent attack that killed 47 people. Haitian security forces have intensified operations, killing a gang leader and targeting other sites, and kidnappings in Port-au-Prince rose in the third quarter. 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Haitisk politi har gjenerobret nasjonalstadion fra gjenger etter to år med kontroll, mens salvadoranske missiler og bakkestyrker angrep et gjengskjul, ødela Mawozo-hovedkvarteret og drepte omtrent 20 gjengmedlemmer, noe som fikk den haitiske statsministeren til å rose president Bukele. FN rapporterte at mer enn 1 000 personer ble drept mellom juli og september, og FN-sjefen fordømte et nylig angrep som drepte 47 personer. Haitiske sikkerhetsstyrker har intensivert operasjonene, drept en gjengleder og rammet andre mål, og kidnappinger i Port-au-Prince økte i tredje kvartal. 193 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
